items.title: The fake news game: actively inoculating against the risk of misinformation

judge.evidence_topic: we developed a ‘fake news game’ in which participants are actively tasked with creating a news article about a strongly politicized issue (the European refugee crisis) using misleading tactics
judge.evidence_empirical: we conducted a randomized field study (N = 95) in a public high school setting.
judge.reason: O artigo trata de um jogo de inoculação (prebunking) contra desinformação, atendendo ao tema. O estudo é empírico, utilizando um experimento de campo randomizado, e o achado informado é sustentado pelo resumo.

items.title: Fake news game confers psychological resistance against online misinformation

judge.evidence_topic: In a novel attempt to address this issue, we designed a psychological intervention in the form of an online browser game. The game draws on an inoculation metaphor, where preemptively exposing, warning, and familiarising people with the strategies used in the production of fake news helps confer cognitive immunity when exposed to real misinformation.
judge.evidence_empirical: We conducted a large-scale evaluation of the game with N = 15,000 participants in a pre-post gameplay design.
judge.reason: O artigo descreve um jogo de inoculação (Bad News) para combater a desinformação, utilizando um desenho pré e pós-intervenção com 15.000 participantes, o que atende aos critérios de inclusão. O estudo não foca em temas proibidos (COVID, vacinas, eleições). O achado principal está diretamente sustentado pelo resumo.

items.title: Good News about Bad News: Gamified Inoculation Boosts Confidence and Cognitive Immunity Against Fake News

judge.evidence_topic: A recent example is the Bad News game, an online fake news game in which players learn about six common misinformation techniques.
judge.evidence_empirical: Using a 2 (treatment vs. control) × 2 (pre vs. post) mixed design (N = 196) we measure participants’ ability to spot misinformation techniques in 18 fake headlines before and after playing Bad News.
judge.reason: O artigo avalia o jogo Bad News, que é um jogo de inoculação contra desinformação, atendendo ao tema. O estudo é empírico (experimento com delineamento misto) e os achados extraídos estão diretamente sustentados pelo resumo.

items.title: Prebunking interventions based on the psychological theory of "inoculation" can reduce susceptibility to misinformation across cultures

judge.evidence_topic: This study finds that the online “fake news” game, Bad News, can confer psychological resistance against common online misinformation strategies (e.g., conspiracy theories, manipulating emotions, political polarization) across different cultures (Sweden, German, Poland, and Greece).
judge.evidence_empirical: This study finds that the online “fake news” game, Bad News, can confer psychological resistance against common online misinformation strategies
judge.reason: O artigo é sobre o jogo Bad News e inoculação, o que está dentro do tema. O estudo é empírico. O achado é sustentado pelo resumo. No entanto, o método (experimentos com desenho pré e pós) não é mencionado no resumo, portanto, o critério method_ok é falso.

items.title: Mixed News about the Bad News Game

judge.evidence_topic: Basol et al. (2020) tested the “the Bad News Game” (BNG), an app designed to improve ability to spot false claims on social media. ... Here, four teams of undergraduate psychology students each attempted an extended replication of Basol et al.
judge.evidence_empirical: four teams of undergraduate psychology students each attempted an extended replication of Basol et al., using updated versions of the original Bad News game.
judge.reason: O artigo descreve um estudo empírico de replicação com coleta de dados novos, não sendo uma reanálise de dados de terceiros. O tema e o método estão alinhados com o pedido.

items.title: Technique-based inoculation against real-world misinformation

judge.evidence_topic: In this study, we address two open questions related to technique-based inoculation in two separate experiments (total n = 2188; convenience sample recruited via the Bad News online game platform)
judge.evidence_empirical: In this study, we address two open questions related to technique-based inoculation in two separate experiments (total n = 2188; convenience sample recruited via the Bad News online game platform)
judge.reason: O artigo descreve um estudo empírico (dois experimentos) utilizando o jogo Bad News para testar a inoculação contra desinformação, atendendo aos critérios de inclusão e não abordando os temas excluídos (COVID-19, vacinas, eleições).

items.title: Long-term effectiveness of inoculation against misinformation: Three longitudinal experiments

judge.evidence_topic: We tested the effectiveness of Bad News, a real-world intervention in which participants develop resistance against misinformation through exposure to weakened doses of misinformation techniques.
judge.evidence_empirical: Using 3 longitudinal experiments (2 preregistered), we tested the effectiveness of Bad News... In 3 experiments (NExp1 = 151, NExp2 = 194, NExp3 = 170), participants played either Bad News (inoculation group) or Tetris (gamified control group)
judge.reason: O artigo avalia o jogo Bad News, que é um jogo de inoculação contra desinformação, atendendo ao critério de tema. O estudo é empírico (experimentos), publicado em periódico e não aborda os temas excluídos (COVID, vacinas, eleições). Os dados extraídos sobre o método e os achados estão corretos e sustentados pelo resumo.

items.title: Feedback exercises boost discernment of misinformation for gamified inoculation interventions

judge.evidence_topic: Gamification is a promising approach to reducing misinformation susceptibility. Previous research has found that 'inoculation' games such as Bad News and Harmony Square help build cognitive resistance against misinformation.
judge.evidence_empirical: We address these issues in two preregistered lab experiments (N1 = 191, N2 = 321) and four quasi-experimental in-game surveys implemented in Harmony Square (N3 = 559) and Bad News (N4 = 2,558, N5 = 419, N6 = 882).
judge.reason: O artigo investiga jogos de inoculação (Bad News e Harmony Square) para combater a desinformação, utilizando métodos empíricos (experimentos e quase-experimentos) sem focar em temas excluídos como COVID-19 ou eleições. O achado principal sobre o impacto dos exercícios de feedback é corroborado pelo resumo.

items.title: Game-based inoculation versus graphic-based inoculation to combat misinformation: a randomized controlled trial

judge.evidence_topic: This study employed inoculation theory and developed an interactive game to help the public counter misinformation.
judge.evidence_empirical: A total of 180 Chinese participants were randomly assigned to game-based inoculation, graphic-based inoculation, and control groups.
judge.reason: O artigo descreve um ensaio controlado randomizado (RCT) que testa um jogo de inoculação contra desinformação, sem focar nos temas excluídos (COVID-19, vacinas, eleições ou política partidária). Os dados extraídos estão corretos e sustentados pelo resumo.

items.title: Gamified Inoculation Against Misinformation in India: A Randomized Control Trial

judge.evidence_topic: We report the results of a game-based intervention against misinformation in India.

judge.reason: O artigo descreve um ensaio controlado randomizado (RCT) de uma intervenção baseada em jogo para inoculação contra desinformação na Índia, atendendo aos critérios de inclusão. O achado extraído reflete fielmente o resultado nulo reportado no resumo.

items.title: Disentangling Item and Testing Effects in Inoculation Research on Online Misinformation: Solomon Revisited

judge.evidence_topic: This study addresses two unanswered methodological questions about a widely adopted online “fake news” inoculation game, Bad News.
judge.evidence_empirical: We investigate both item and testing effects in two online studies (total N = 2,159) using the Bad News game.
judge.reason: O artigo utiliza o jogo Bad News para investigar efeitos de inoculação, o que está dentro do escopo. O estudo é empírico (dois estudos online) e o método (Solomon's Three Group Design) está corretamente descrito. O achado principal é sustentado pelo resumo.

items.title: How to "inoculate" against multimodal misinformation: A conceptual replication of Roozenbeek and van der Linden (2020)

judge.evidence_topic: We developed a game called Cat Park , in which players learn about five manipulation techniques (trolling, emotional manipulation, amplification, polarization, and conspiracism), and how misinformation can spread through images.
judge.evidence_empirical: To test the game’s efficacy, we conducted a conceptual replication ( N = 380) of Roozenbeek and van der Linden’s 2020 study about Harmony Square , with the same study design, item set, and hypotheses.
judge.reason: O artigo descreve um estudo empírico (replicação conceitual) sobre um jogo de inoculação (Cat Park) contra desinformação, sem abordar os temas excluídos (COVID-19, vacinas, eleições ou política). Os dados extraídos estão corretos e sustentados pelo resumo.

items.title: Misinformation Is Contagious: Middle school students learn how to evaluate and share information responsibly through a digital game
Bad News in the civics classroom: How serious gameplay fosters teenagers' ability to discern misinformation techniques

judge.evidence_topic: Although the serious game Bad News has been used to inoculate citizens against misinformation, it has not been formally evaluated in traditional classrooms. We therefore evaluated its impact on 516 upper-secondary Swedish students playing individually, paired, or with the whole class.
judge.evidence_empirical: We therefore evaluated its impact on 516 upper-secondary Swedish students playing individually, paired, or with the whole class.
judge.reason: O artigo avalia o jogo Bad News em um contexto educacional (sala de aula), o que se enquadra no tema de jogos de inoculação contra desinformação. O estudo é empírico, com 516 participantes, e o método de pré e pós-intervenção é confirmado pelo resumo. O achado principal é uma paráfrase direta do resultado apresentado no resumo.

items.title: Investigating the long-term impact of misinformation interventions in upper secondary education

judge.evidence_topic: we tested three types of interventions: prebunking through the Bad News game, fact-checking skills via the News Evaluator workshop, and subject-specific disciplinary literacy interventions.

judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico experimental que testa o jogo Bad News para combater a desinformação, sem abordar os temas excluídos (COVID-19, vacinas, eleições ou política partidária). O achado extraído reflete fielmente o resultado relatado no resumo.

items.title: Chaos creator

judge.evidence_topic: Via a quasi-experimental study, this research explores the effect of prebunking techniques in an IL instruction session on undergraduate students’ ability to recognise misinformation. The prebunking techniques are delivered through a competitive game called Chaos Creator, based on the Bad News game developed by researchers at Cambridge University.
judge.evidence_empirical: Via a quasi-experimental study, this research explores the effect of prebunking techniques in an IL instruction session on undergraduate students’ ability to recognise misinformation.
judge.reason: O artigo descreve um estudo quase-experimental utilizando um jogo de inoculação (Chaos Creator) para letramento informacional, o que se enquadra nos critérios. O achado principal é sustentado pelo resumo.

judge.evidence_topic: The aim of this study is to address this gap by examining whether pre-service teachers can learn about fake news using the augmented reality escape game Escape Fake.

judge.reason: O artigo descreve um experimento com 373 participantes comparando um jogo online (intervenção ativa) com um folheto (intervenção passiva) para inoculação contra desinformação, o que se enquadra no tema.
